name: XLOOKUP
what: Find one value in a list and return its matching value from another column. It can look left or right.
read: XLOOKUP(what to find, where to look, what to return, what to show if not found).
data: WorkID IT-001 in column A; Owner in column F.
result: Ayesha Khan
error: #N/A when the WorkID does not exist.
fix: Add the 4th argument, "Not Found", or wrap with IFNA / IFERROR.
benefit: One lookup replaces VLOOKUP + INDEX-MATCH for most daily work, and it does not break when a column is inserted.

name: VLOOKUP
what: Classic lookup. It looks in the FIRST column of a table and returns a value from a column to its right.
read: VLOOKUP(what, table, which column number, FALSE for exact match). Always use FALSE for exact work.
data: Table A:B, WorkID in A, Project in B.
result: Customer Portal Revamp
error: #N/A if not found; #REF! if the column number is larger than the table.
fix: Use FALSE, count the column number from the table start, and wrap with IFERROR for a clean message.
benefit: Works in every Excel version, including old files your office still uses.

name: INDEX-MATCH
what: Two functions together. MATCH finds the row number, INDEX returns the value from that row.
read: MATCH finds WHERE it is. INDEX gives WHAT is there.
data: DueDate in column M; WorkID in column A.
error: #N/A if the WorkID is missing; wrong result if MATCH uses 1 instead of 0.
fix: Always use 0 for exact match in MATCH, and check that both ranges have the same number of rows.
benefit: It can look left, right, up or down, and it does not break when columns move. Use it when VLOOKUP cannot reach the value.

name: MATCH
what: Returns the POSITION of a value in a list, not the value itself.
read: MATCH(what, where, 0). The answer is a number like 1, 2 or 3.
data: IT-001 is the first data row.
error: #N/A if the value is not in the list, or if there is an extra space in the text.
fix: Use TRIM on pasted text, and use 0 for exact match.
benefit: It is the engine inside INDEX-MATCH, and it is useful for checking whether an ID exists at all.

name: SUMIF
what: Add values that meet ONE condition.
read: SUMIF(where to check, condition, what to add). Note: the sum range comes LAST here.
data: Project in B; Actual Hours in J.
result: Actual hours for Inventory API only (see workbook 9_MIS_REPORT for the live total).
error: 0 or a wrong total, usually because the criteria text does not match exactly, or the ranges are different sizes.
fix: Copy the criteria text from the data itself, and keep both ranges the same height.
benefit: One-line totals by project, owner or status, without filtering and adding by hand.

name: SUMIFS
what: Add values that meet MULTIPLE conditions at the same time.
read: SUMIFS(what to add, check 1, condition 1, check 2, condition 2). Note: the sum range comes FIRST here, opposite to SUMIF.
data: Actual Hours in J; Project in B; Sprint in D.
result: Actual hours for HRMS Upgrade in Sprint 2 only.
error: 0 when one condition does not match, or when a number is typed as text.
fix: Test each condition alone first, then combine them. Check that Sprint is a number, not text.
benefit: This is the formula behind Pivot-style matrices and most dashboard totals.

name: COUNTIF
what: Count cells that meet ONE condition.
read: COUNTIF(where to check, condition).
data: Status in column G, 120 rows.
error: 0 when the status text has a different spelling, space or case in pasted data.
fix: Use the exact status text, or better, use a Data Validation dropdown so spelling stays clean.
benefit: Instant counts for KPIs: how many delayed, completed, blocked, without counting by hand.

name: COUNTIFS
what: Count rows that meet MULTIPLE conditions at the same time.
read: COUNTIFS(check 1, condition 1, check 2, condition 2).
data: Status in G; Priority in H. IT-005 is one example: Delayed + Critical.
result: Delayed + Critical tasks only (live count in the workbook).
error: 0 when the two conditions never occur together, or when ranges are different sizes.
fix: Check each condition with COUNTIF alone first, then combine.
benefit: This is how escalation lists are counted: Delayed AND Critical, Blocked AND High, and so on.

name: AVERAGEIF
what: Average values that meet ONE condition.
read: AVERAGEIF(where to check, condition, what to average).
data: Status in G; Actual Hours in J.
result: Average actual hours for Completed tasks only.
error: Wrong average when blank or text cells are mixed in, or when the criteria does not match.
fix: Check the criteria spelling, and remember that blanks are ignored in an average.
benefit: Useful for effort norms: on average, how long does a completed task actually take?

name: AVERAGEIFS
what: Average values that meet MULTIPLE conditions.
read: AVERAGEIFS(what to average, check 1, condition 1, check 2, condition 2).
data: Variance in K; Project in B; Status in G.
result: Average variance for Delayed tasks in Customer Portal Revamp only.
error: #DIV/0! when no row meets all conditions, because there is nothing to average.
fix: Wrap with IFERROR, and check with COUNTIFS that at least one row matches.
benefit: Fair comparisons: average overrun for one project and one status, not mixed with everything else.

name: IF
what: Choose between two results based on a test.
read: IF(test, if yes, if no).
example: =IF(K4>3, "Overdue", "On Track")  where K is Variance Hours
data: IT-005 variance is +5.0 hours, so the test is TRUE.
result: Overdue
error: Wrong label when the comparison sign is reversed, or when text and numbers are mixed.
fix: Read the test out loud first: 'Is variance greater than 3?' Then write it.
benefit: Every flag, label and RAG colour in a report starts with IF.

name: IFS
what: Test several conditions in order, without nesting IF inside IF.
read: IFS(test 1, result 1, test 2, result 2, TRUE, fallback). Excel stops at the first TRUE test.
data: Status in G; Variance in K.
result: Green for Completed, Red for large overrun, Amber for small overrun, otherwise Green.
error: #N/A when no condition is TRUE and there is no TRUE fallback at the end.
fix: Always end IFS with TRUE and a default value.
benefit: RAG ratings become readable. Nested IF becomes hard to read after three levels; IFS stays clean.

name: AND / OR
what: Combine tests. AND needs ALL tests TRUE. OR needs ANY test TRUE.
read: AND = sab shartein poori hon. OR = koi aik shart poori ho.
data: IT-005: Status Delayed, Priority Critical, so AND is TRUE.
result: ESCALATE
error: ESCALATE never appears when one test uses the wrong column or spelling.
fix: Test each condition in its own cell first, then combine them with AND / OR.
benefit: Escalation rules are exactly this: Delayed AND Critical, Blocked OR Overdue, and so on.

name: IFERROR
what: Show a friendly value instead of any error.
read: IFERROR(try this, if it fails show this).
data: IT-999 does not exist in the data.
result: Not Found
error: Hiding a REAL error, like a wrong range, because IFERROR hides every error type.
fix: For lookups only, prefer IFNA (see unit 41). Use IFERROR for division and dashboard totals where 0 is safe.
benefit: Dashboards stay clean for managers. One #N/A should not break a whole report.

name: TEXT
what: Show a number or date as formatted TEXT.
read: TEXT(value, "format"). Common formats: "DD-MMM-YYYY", "MMM-YYYY", "0.0%".
data: IT-001 DueDate is 20-May-2025.
error: Result cannot be used in maths, because TEXT returns text, not a date or number.
fix: Use TEXT only for display and titles. Keep the original date cell for calculations.
benefit: Report titles, month labels and MIS headings look professional and update automatically.

name: CONCAT / &
what: Join text from several cells into one label.
read: Use & between pieces, with "text" in quotes for separators.
data: A4 = IT-001, B4 = Customer Portal Revamp.
result: IT-001 - Customer Portal Revamp
error: Numbers may show without formatting, for example a date becomes a serial number like 45777.
fix: For dates inside a label, wrap the date with TEXT first.
benefit: Clean IDs, titles and email subjects, built automatically from the data.

name: LEFT / MID / RIGHT
what: Take characters from the left, middle or right of a text value.
read: LEFT = shuru se. RIGHT = akhir se. MID = beech se, start position aur length ke saath.
error: Wrong piece when the text length changes, for example IT-1001 vs IT-001.
fix: For variable lengths, combine with FIND or use TEXTSPLIT in newer Excel, and test with the longest code.
benefit: Split codes, prefixes and IDs from imported data without retyping.

name: LEN / TRIM / UPPER
what: LEN counts characters. TRIM removes extra spaces. UPPER makes capitals. PROPER capitalises each word.
read: First clean with TRIM, then check with LEN, then format with UPPER or PROPER.
data: Messy name with extra spaces.
result: Ayesha Khan
error: Lookup fails even though the name 'looks' the same, because of a hidden space.
fix: Always TRIM pasted names and IDs before a lookup or COUNTIF.
benefit: Most 'formula not working' problems are actually dirty data. Cleaning first saves hours.

name: DATE / MONTH / YEAR
what: DATE builds a real date from numbers. MONTH and YEAR pull parts out of a date.
read: DATE(saal, mahina, din). MONTH(date) gives 1 to 12. YEAR(date) gives the year.
example: =MONTH(M4)  where M is DueDate for IT-001
data: DueDate 20-May-2025.
error: MONTH on text that only looks like a date returns #VALUE!.
fix: Make sure the cell is a real Excel date, not text. Use DATEVALUE or retype as a date if needed.
benefit: Monthly grouping, monthly MIS and ageing all depend on real dates and MONTH/YEAR.

name: EOMONTH
what: Last day of a month, a number of months ahead or behind.
read: EOMONTH(date, 0) = same month-end. EOMONTH(date, 1) = next month-end.
data: Report date 30-Jun-2025.
error: Wrong month-end when the start cell is text, not a date.
fix: Use a real date cell, and check with MONTH that the result month is correct.
benefit: Month-end MIS, period closing and monthly cut-offs become one formula, no calendar lookup.

name: NETWORKDAYS
what: Count WORKING days between two dates, skipping Saturdays and Sundays.
read: NETWORKDAYS(start, end). Add a holidays list as the third argument for public holidays.
example: =NETWORKDAYS(L4, M4)  Start to Due for IT-001
data: Start 12-May-2025, Due 20-May-2025.
result: 7 working days (12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 19, 20 May, skipping the weekend).
error: Off-by-one, because NETWORKDAYS counts both the start and end days.
fix: For 'days overdue after the due date', subtract 1, as shown on sheet 10_SLA_AGEING.
benefit: SLA in working days is fair. Calendar days punish a team for weekends.

name: UNIQUE
what: List each value once, with duplicates removed. The result SPILLS into neighbouring cells.
read: UNIQUE(list). Type it once, Excel fills the list below.
data: Project column, 120 rows, 4 projects repeated.
result: Customer Portal Revamp, HRMS Upgrade, Inventory API, Service Desk Migration (4 rows, spilling down).
error: #SPILL! when a cell below the formula already has a value.
fix: Clear the cells below the formula. Never type over a spill range.
benefit: Dropdown lists, summary labels and distinct counts, without manual copy-paste and deduplication.

name: SORT / SORTBY
what: Return a SORTED copy of a list or table, without changing the original data.
read: SORT(list, which column, 1 for A-Z / -1 for largest first).
data: IT data A:K; column 11 is Variance Hours.
result: Tasks sorted by variance, largest overrun first.
error: #SPILL! if the spill area is blocked; wrong order if sort_order is 1 instead of -1.
fix: Clear the spill area, and use -1 for descending, largest first.
benefit: Top 10 overruns, latest tasks, or biggest risks, always live, never re-sorted by hand.

name: FILTER
what: Return ONLY the rows that meet a condition. The result spills.
read: FILTER(what to show, test, what to show if nothing matches). Multiply tests for AND.
data: Status in G; Priority in H.
result: Only Delayed + Critical rows, spilling down. IT-005 is in this list.
error: #CALC! when nothing matches and no if_empty text is given.
fix: Always give an if_empty message like "None found".
benefit: Live escalation lists, overdue lists and blocked lists, no manual filtering and copying.

name: MAX / MIN / LARGE / SMALL
what: MAX = largest. MIN = smallest. LARGE = k-th largest. SMALL = k-th smallest.
read: LARGE(range, 3) = 3rd largest. SMALL(range, 1) = smallest.
data: Variance Hours in K.
result: 3rd largest variance (worst overruns ranked 1, 2, 3).
error: #NUM! when k is larger than the number of values.
fix: Check k against COUNT of the range first.
benefit: Worst bottlenecks and best cases in one formula, for SLA review and weekly top-5 lists.

name: RANK
what: Rank a number inside a list. Order 0 = largest is rank 1. Order 1 = smallest is rank 1.
read: RANK(this number, whole list, 0). Lock the list with $ so it does not move when copied.
example: =RANK(D22, $D$22:$D$25, 0)  on MIS project summary, D = Delayed count
data: Project delayed counts: Customer Portal 5, HRMS 6, Inventory 3, Service Desk 4.
result: HRMS Upgrade ranks 1 (most delayed), Inventory API ranks 4 (fewest delayed).
error: Wrong ranks when the list range moves as the formula is copied down.
fix: Lock the list with $ signs: $D$22:$D$25.
benefit: Rank projects, owners or sprints by delay, overrun or completion, for a management table.

name: PERCENTILE
what: Value below which k percent of values fall. k is 0 to 1.
read: PERCENTILE(range, 0.95) = 95th percentile.
data: Actual Hours in J, 120 items.
result: 95th percentile of actual hours - the SLA upper bound (live value in 9_MIS_REPORT).
error: #NUM! when k is below 0 or above 1.
fix: Keep k between 0 and 1, for example 0.95, not 95.
benefit: SLA caps should use percentiles, not just averages. One huge task should not hide the normal range.

name: Relative / Absolute / Mixed References
what: Control what moves when a formula is copied. $ locks a row, a column, or both.
read: A1 moves both ways. $A$1 never moves. $A1 locks the column only. A$1 locks the row only.
example: =B6*$B$3  where B3 is the hourly rate
data: Planned Hours in B; rate in yellow cell B3 on sheet 6_REFERENCES.
result: Cost stays correct when copied down, because $B$3 never moves. Without $, B3 becomes B4, B5 and the cost breaks.
error: Totals suddenly change after copying, because a fixed cell moved.
fix: Press F4 on a reference to cycle: A1, $A$1, A$1, $A1, A1. Choose the lock before copying.
benefit: This is the most important Excel skill for dashboards. Every matrix and cost table depends on it.

name: Pivot via SUMIFS / COUNTIFS
syntax: SUMIFS / COUNTIFS matrix: rows = Project, columns = Sprint
what: Rebuild a Pivot Table result with live formulas, so no Refresh is needed.
read: Each cell is COUNTIFS(Project = row, Sprint = column) or SUMIFS for hours.
data: Project in B; Sprint in D; row label in A; sprint label in row 3.
result: Project x Sprint matrix on sheet 5_PIVOT_SIM. Each project has 30 items in total.
error: Matrix does not update when a new project appears, because the row labels are typed, not UNIQUE.
fix: For a fully live matrix, build row labels with UNIQUE, or add the new project row and copy the formula across.
benefit: Dashboard matrices that update the moment source data changes, without clicking Refresh.

name: Data Validation
syntax: Data -> Data Validation -> List / Whole number / Decimal / Date
what: Stop bad data entering the sheet. Dropdowns, number ranges and date rules, with an error alert.
read: Select the cells, choose Allow, type the list or range, set an error alert on Stop.
example: Status dropdown: Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Delayed, Blocked, On Hold
data: Sheet 8_DATA_VALIDATION, yellow cells B4:B9.
result: Typing 'done' instead of 'Completed' is stopped, so COUNTIF("Completed") keeps working.
error: Formulas still count wrong when validation was added AFTER bad data was already typed.
fix: Add validation first, then clean old data with TRIM and Find & Replace, then re-check with COUNTIF.
benefit: Garbage in, garbage out. Validation is what protects every dashboard downstream.

name: Conditional Formatting
syntax: Home -> Conditional Formatting -> Highlight Cells / Colour Scales / Data Bars / Formula Rule
what: Colour cells automatically from their values. No manual colouring.
read: Rule first: 'If Status = Delayed, fill red.' Then apply to the whole column.
example: Status Delayed = red fill; Completed = green fill; Variance = 3-colour scale
data: Sheet 7_CONDITIONAL_FORMATTING, and Status/Variance on 1_IT_PM_DATA.
result: Delayed rows jump out in red, completed in green, worst variance in red on the scale.
error: Colours do not update, because cells were coloured by hand instead of by a rule, or the rule range is too small.
fix: Use Manage Rules to check the range and order. Rules run top to bottom; first match can win.
benefit: Managers see problems in seconds, without reading 120 rows.

name: Power Query
syntax: Data -> Get Data -> From Folder / From File -> Transform -> Close & Load
what: Excel's built-in ETL: Extract, Transform, Load. Combine and clean files, then refresh in one click.
read: Month-end flow: new files land in a folder -> Power Query picks them up -> steps run -> master table loads.
example: Append Jan, Feb, Mar ... Jun exports into one master table, then Pivot and dashboard formulas refresh.
data: Concept demo in the Word guide, Section 12. No monthly CSV files were supplied with this package, so this is a steps demo, not a live file demo.
result: Refresh time under a minute, instead of hours of copy-paste, for a monthly MIS.
error: Refresh fails when a source file is renamed, moved, or a column header changes.
fix: Keep file names and headers stable, keep one folder for inputs, and check the Applied Steps list after a failed refresh.
benefit: The single biggest time saver for a monthly MIS: repeatable cleaning, not repeatable manual work.

name: TODAY  [NEW]
what: Today's date, updating every time the file is opened or recalculated.
read: TODAY() takes no arguments. Just type =TODAY().
example: Days overdue = ReportDate - DueDate, where ReportDate can be =TODAY() in live use
data: Sheet 10_SLA_AGEING uses a fixed ReportDate 30-Jun-2025 for training, so results repeat. In live use, replace it with TODAY().
result: On 30-Jun-2025, IT-002 (Due 10-May-2025, not completed) is 51 calendar days overdue.
error: A report changes every day, so yesterday's printed MIS no longer matches today's file.
fix: For a frozen report, paste TODAY() as a value, or keep a separate ReportDate cell and note the date on the report.
benefit: Ageing, overdue and SLA reports stay live without anyone typing today's date.

name: WORKDAY  [NEW]
what: A date that many WORKING days ahead (or behind, with a negative number), skipping weekends.
read: WORKDAY(start, how many working days).
example: =WORKDAY(M4, 1)  where M is DueDate for IT-001
data: DueDate 20-May-2025 was a Tuesday.
result: 21-May-2025 (next working day).
error: Wrong date when holidays are not listed, or when workdays is typed as a date.
fix: Keep a small holidays list and pass it as the third argument for real SLA work.
benefit: Deadlines in working days: '5 working days to fix' becomes an exact date, not a guess.

name: EDATE  [NEW]
what: Same day of the month, a number of months ahead or behind.
read: EDATE(date, months). Positive = future, negative = past.
example: =EDATE(M4, 1)  where M is DueDate for IT-001
data: DueDate 20-May-2025.
error: Month-end edge: EDATE(31-Jan, 1) gives 28-Feb (or 29-Feb in a leap year), not 31-Feb, which does not exist.
fix: That is correct behaviour, not an error. Use EOMONTH if you always want month-end.
benefit: Review dates, renewal dates and monthly follow-ups, one formula ahead.

name: DATEDIF  [NEW]
what: Whole days, months or years between two dates. DATEDIF is a hidden Excel function: it works, but Excel does not list it in the function wizard.
read: DATEDIF(start, end, "d" for days, "m" for months, "y" for years).
example: =DATEDIF(L4, M4, "d")  Start to Due for IT-001
data: Start 12-May-2025, Due 20-May-2025.
result: 8 days
error: #NUM! when the start date is after the end date.
fix: Check the order: start first, end second. Swap them if the result is negative in your head.
benefit: Task age, tenure and SLA age in exact days or months, for ageing reports.

name: SWITCH  [NEW]
what: Match ONE value against several cases and return the matching result. Cleaner than nested IF when you test the same cell many times.
read: SWITCH(cell, case 1, result 1, case 2, result 2, default).
data: Status in G. IT-001 is Completed.
error: Default value appears when the status spelling does not match any case exactly.
fix: Use the exact status text, or use Data Validation so spelling stays clean.
benefit: Status codes, priority codes and category codes become readable in one line.

name: TEXTJOIN  [NEW]
what: Join many cells or values with a separator, optionally skipping blanks.
read: TEXTJOIN(separator, TRUE to skip blanks, values...).
data: Three blocker notes, one blank in the middle.
result: Login bug, API delay
error: Extra separators when ignore_empty is FALSE and a blank is included.
fix: Set ignore_empty to TRUE for lists like blockers, owners or tags.
benefit: One-line summaries: all blockers, all owners, all tags for a project, in a single cell.

name: SUMPRODUCT  [NEW]
what: Multiply matching pairs, then add them up. For weighted averages, divide by the sum of the weights.
read: SUMPRODUCT(weights, values) / SUM(weights).
data: Story Points in O (weights); %Complete in P (values).
result: Story-point weighted % complete for the whole portfolio (live value in 9_MIS_REPORT). A simple average would give small and large tasks equal weight, which is wrong.
error: #VALUE! when the two ranges are different sizes, or when a cell contains text instead of a number.
fix: Keep both ranges the same height, and check that Story Points and %Complete are numbers, not text.
benefit: The honest progress number: a 8-point task counts more than a 1-point task.

name: COUNTBLANK  [NEW]
what: Count EMPTY cells in a range.
read: COUNTBLANK(range). A cell with a space is NOT blank; a truly empty cell is.
data: FinishDate in N. Only Completed tasks have a FinishDate in this dataset.
result: 72 (120 total minus 48 completed = 72 unfinished, with no FinishDate yet).
error: Count is too low when 'blank' cells actually contain a space or a formula returning "".
fix: Clean spaces with TRIM, and remember that a formula returning "" is counted by COUNTBLANK in Excel, but looks blank to the eye.
benefit: Completeness checks: how many tasks have no finish date, no owner, no due date? That is data quality in one number.

name: IFNA  [NEW]
what: Catch ONLY #N/A, and let every other error show. That is the difference from IFERROR.
read: IFNA(try this, if #N/A show this).
data: IT-999 does not exist.
result: Not Found
error: A wrong range still shows its real error, for example #REF! or #VALUE!, instead of being hidden.
fix: That is the point. Fix the range error; do not hide it with IFERROR.
benefit: Safer lookups: missing IDs get a clean message, but real mistakes stay visible for you to fix.

name: SUBSTITUTE / CLEAN  [NEW]
what: SUBSTITUTE replaces text. CLEAN removes non-printable characters from pasted or imported data.
read: SUBSTITUTE(text, what to replace, replacement). CLEAN(text) needs only the text.
data: Code pasted with spaces around the dash.
error: SUBSTITUTE replaces EVERY occurrence by default, not just the first one, unless you give an instance number.
fix: For only the first occurrence, add the instance number as the 4th argument.
benefit: Fix imported IDs, codes and names in bulk, without Find & Replace breaking other columns.
